01 / Less reconstruction. More continuation.

Your work has context.
Keep it close.

When you come back to a project, the first job shouldn’t be remembering what the last job was. Cockpit puts the conversation, the current files and the next decision within reach.

01

Cockpit 0.1.7 / Prerelease

Your next session
starts here.

Already building with Claude Code or Codex? Try a workspace that keeps the project together. This is an early build, ready for hands-on feedback.

Download for Mac ↓Release notes ↗SHA-256 ↗

Apple silicon (M1+) · DMG · 128.4 MB
Not notarized. The Terminal install below opens without the Gatekeeper block.

What you’ll need

  • 01 A Mac with Apple silicon.
    Intel, Windows and Linux aren’t supported.
  • 02 A current Claude Code or Codex CLI, installed and signed in, for the simplest first run.
  • 03 Your own agent access.
    Provider subscriptions and limits still apply.
01 / INSTALL

Install Cockpit.

Paste this into Terminal:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Holodeck23/agent-cockpit/main/install.sh | sh

It shows the beta terms and installs Cockpit into Applications after you type agree. Or open the DMG and drag Cockpit into Applications.

02 / FIRST LAUNCH

Allow the first launch.

Installed from Terminal, Cockpit opens on the first try. From the DMG, Cockpit shows the beta terms when it first opens, and if macOS blocks the app, choose Done. Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway, authenticate, then confirm.

03 / PICK UP YOUR WORK

Resume. See the result.

Open a project folder and choose Resume and show me the app. No recent conversation? Explore the project or try the sample. Review the startup approval, then try the preview.

Before you install

A few good
questions.

Where is the full feature list?

Open the feature directory above (through v0.1.5; the v0.1.6 and v0.1.7 release notes list what is new), or read the user guide on GitHub. The list covers the downloadable prerelease; features on development branches are added after they ship.

Does Cockpit include an AI subscription?

No. Cockpit runs the agent CLIs you install and sign into: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and OpenCode (including configured OpenRouter models). Usage is billed or counted by those providers. Cockpit doesn’t supply model access or bypass usage limits.

Where does my work go?

Projects stay in the folders you choose. Cockpit keeps conversation metadata, events and readable Markdown transcripts under ~/.agent-cockpit/ on your Mac. Prompts and attached context go to your selected agent’s provider. There is no Cockpit cloud account or cloud storage. One exception, as a condition of the beta: crash and error reports go to Cockpit’s developer through Sentry (EU region), with no setting to turn them off. A report holds the error and its stack trace, Cockpit’s version and the macOS version and kind of Mac. Your home folder is replaced with ~; file contents, screenshots and the machine name are never sent, though error text can name a project or file. See the beta terms.

What should I expect from the prerelease?

v0.1.7 makes approvals clearer (a countdown and one plain outcome per request), shows the permission level and where a message goes, shows images Antigravity generates, and fixes a Codex Stop race and two clicks that could go missing. v0.1.6 added worktrees (an agent can work on its own copy of the project and merge back), account profiles, so a project can use a different Claude Code or Codex account, a handoff you see before switching agents, the live preview on your phone, Report a bug and Send feedback, the one-line Terminal install and crash reports. Check for Updates (since v0.1.3) offers the install command, or the download, and you install it yourself. Its Claude compatibility check passed same-Mac acceptance on a second account in v0.1.2. It isn’t notarized. An outside tester installed an earlier build; independent other-Mac acceptance of this version is still open. Three automated fresh-state runs with a signed-in Claude CLI reached an inspected sample app in 19.9–22.9 seconds; your project and setup may take longer. OpenCode’s live OpenRouter path remains unverified. Antigravity gets Cockpit’s tools only in projects where you turn them on. Read the full release notes before installing.

Can I check in from my phone?

Optional phone access uses your own Tailscale account. Pair your phone to follow conversations, reply, approve requests and stop a turn. Keep your Mac awake and Cockpit running. Physical-phone push notification delivery is not yet verified.

How do workflows run?

Save instructions and agent settings, then run them manually, on an interval, daily, on weekdays, or on selected days at a local time. Cockpit must be running. After downtime, at most one missed run starts when you reopen it; failed runs report their errors and do not block future scheduled runs.

Is this related to Enjoy?

Cockpit is an independent project inspired by Enjoy’s layout and interaction model. It is not affiliated with Enjoy. Cockpit’s code, name, mark and copy are its own; no Enjoy code or assets were taken.
